The name of this modifier needs to be intended to show that it never scales bones, but rather repositions joints. Because scaling bones causes features like IK to be broken the behavior, we need to avoid names that imply scaling. Also, since it functions on its own, names related to Skin are not considered desirable.

Initially it was BoneExpander, but since that strongly gave the impression of performing scaling, it became Spreader, which strictly represents its action, that meaning that in 1 vs n bones, the position is "spread" by the value set in this node.

In other words, it's a position converter from scale. A name like "Scl2PosConverter3D" would probably be ideal, but it would break consistency with other Godot nodes. And the "Disperser" cannot be used because it is already in use by "BoneTwistDisperser3D".

But, this is accurate. For example, if you change the width of the hand using `skin_scale`, you'll need to widen the spacing between the fingers. `BoneSpreader3D` serves the purpose of widening that spacing.
So the angle between the fingers changes? Not the relative positions
The angle remains the same. Even if you widen the "hand" skin, the roots of the fingers will remain in their original positions. BoneSpreader adjusts the position to increase the space between them.
The angle is what I meant by a "v", "spread" as opposed to "spread out", like spreading a fan or a hand of cards or an umbrella
Although the property's value “bone_pose_rotation“ remains unchanged, this means that the apparent angle of the line connecting the parent bone to the child bone will actually be spread.

"Extender" was a candidate in the past, but I decided against it because it brings to mind scaling. I think we could distinguish it if it included "Offset", but since it doesn't apply an offset to a single bone, that would result in a very long class name: `ChildBoneOffsetExtender3D`.

Basically, what makes this a bit confusing is that, while it appears to be a scaling of the parent bone, what’s actually being applied is a change in the position of the child bone. So far, I personally feel that `ChildBoneShifter3D` is the short and most accurate.

I'm a native US English speaker, and while "BoneSpreader" doesn't conjure _gruesome_ imagery for me, the early-morning immature side of myself does go to some... perhaps undesirable places with it 😅

_Edit: After posting this I decided to go look up "bone spreader" to see how much of an existing definition it had. Looks like it is indeed some kind of gnarly-looking medical tool. It'd be important to keep in mind that if people look up "godot bone spreader" when trying to find docs, they're likely to collide with those results as well._

To go over the main options I see here so far:

- "BoneSpreader" - Less bad as I think about it more. As previously stated, it doesn't stick out to me as "gruesome" per se, any more than other "bone" related names.
- "BoneDistributor" - Could potentially suggest the idea of generating bones and sending them to other nodes. I generally do like "distributor" in the sense of distributing an existing collection of items among an area. FWIW some programs use the term "distribute" to refer to placing items in a space together. See Affinity Designer 2 here:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/684cb268-0678-45c6-9221-aed83b5182ce

- "BoneRepositioner" - While it describes the behavior, the name seems a bit too generic and vague to me. The other names provide a better suggestion of what kind of repositioning it would be doing.
- "BoneShifter" - Good for not suggesting a scaling operation is occurring. Overall feels similar to "BoneSpreader" to me, but with more emphasis on not scaling.
- "BoneSplayer" - As a native English speaker, this feels relatively intuitive to me and describes the operation well (assuming I correctly understand the operation, of course). But I do agree with AST that it's a bit unusual of a word, and thus could be unintuitive to non-native speakers or even native speakers who aren't very familiar with unusual words.

I'd like to throw a few other suggestions into the mix.
- When I recorded the Affinity Designer video, I saw it used the term "space", as in "space horizontally".  I think "BoneSpacer" could work.
- "BoneMargin" might also be workable, as "margins" are known as the space that elements have between themselves and other elements or edges of a page etc.

While I believe that "spreader" is probably the most apt word for what it does, maybe "displacer" works as a substitute?
(Non-native english speaker)

Indeed, to me, BoneSpaceAdjuster3D sounds like a node that changes a bone from local space to world space, but that's not what this node does.

If we can't come up with a name creatively, we could use a name that describes what it does mechanically. for example SkinScaleApplier3D or BoneSkinScaler3D or BoneSkinScalePositioner3D.

BoneSkinScaleAdjuster3D or BoneScaleAdjuster3D could also work, though it is a bit misleading because this node does not adjust the skin scale, but the other way around.

The Add Node screen has some usability issues that make it difficult to navigate nodes deep in the inheritance hierarchy so I imagine users will often use the search bar to find nodes. For this reason, it would help for the node name to have some relation to the property names.

BoneDisplacer? or BoneDisplacement?

We will never adopt "Displacer".

To explain the function again to someone who knows nothing about behavior, the modifier moves the position of a child bone’s root by scaling the parent bone’s root as the pivot (it’s repositioning, not scaling). And you can use `skin_scale` as the scale via an option, but you can also set any other scale. In addition, the scale can be expanded or shrunk. In other words, if we were to describe this function in a single word, it would be "adjust" or "reposition".
Please just upload some visualization of what it does, the descriptions of what it does is not effective
However, this scaling does not affect the skin, nor is it propagated to children. Child bones are only repositioned.

Then "space adjuster" would be more appropriate as it "spreads out" as opposed to "spreads", doesn't "splay" (that would mean rotating the fingers so the tips remain the same angle with the previous bone, not remaining equidistant), so repositioning
